faq.title: Frequently asked questions

q1.q: Is it easy to set up and adapt to my working method?
q1.a: Yes. You can start simply (one session, one student) then structure it gradually. The tool adapts to your way of coaching: you keep your settings, your organization and your habits, but with a clearer and more professional framework.

q2.q: Is this really useful for students?
q2.a: Yes, because the student does not need to understand your organization: he follows a guided, clear and structured session. Result: fewer errors, more regularity, and progress that is easier to visualize.

q3.q: Is it compatible with remote coaching, at home and in the classroom?
q3.a: Yes. You can coach face-to-face, by video or leave the student independently. In all cases, the calendar, history and progress remain centralized.

q4.q: What happens at the end of the 14 days?
q4.a: You will have had time to test the tool with your real routine. The trial is without a credit card: you choose the suite only if you see real value (time saving, clarity, professional rendering).

about.title: About
about.intro:
Boost Your Life is the platform designed for modern coaches, whether they support their clients in person or remotely.

Today, customers expect much more than a simple program: they want structured progression, clear follow-up and professional experience.

Boost Your Life allows you to offer this, simply and efficiently.

mission.title: Why this platform exists
mission.body:
Coaching is evolving. Customer expectations too. 

Many coaches still work with scattered files, PDF sent manually or tools poorly suited to managing several clients.

This takes time, complicates monitoring and limits professional perception.  

Boost Your Life was designed to structure modern coaching and provide a clear, coherent and scalable system.

features.title: How the platform supports you
items: Centralisation de tous vos clients au même endroit
Organisation claire des séances (temps, consignes, variantes)
Suivi précis des performances et de l’évolution
Un outil adapté au coaching en présentiel comme à distance

autonomy.title: You remain the coach
autonomy.body:
Boost Your Life does not replace your expertise. 
He strengthens it.

The platform acts like a structuring assistant: it automates certain tasks, clarifies the organization and allows you to concentrate on the essentials — support and the relationship with your customers.

You maintain control, vision and decision.

vision.title: Our vision
vision.body:
We believe that modern coaching must rely on modern tools.

Our ambition is to become a reference for independent coaches who wish to structure, professionalize and develop their activity.

Coaching is no longer based solely on technical competence, but also on the ability to offer a clear, measurable and coherent experience.

Boost Your Life is part of this evolution. 

The platform continually evolves in order to adapt to the needs of coaches and realities on the ground.

why.title: What this actually changes
items: Un gain de temps sur la gestion administrative
Une progression plus claire et mesurable
Une structure qui renforce la confiance des clients
Un système adapté au coaching moderne

base-alimentation.title: Diet Basics
base-alimentation.summary: Simple guidelines to understand how to build a consistent eating day.

keyPoints.0: A balanced main meal ideally combines a source of protein, vegetables, a portion of starchy foods and a dose of fat.
keyPoints.1: Vegetables provide volume, fiber, micronutrients and satiety; they can be raw or cooked depending on digestive tolerance.
keyPoints.2: Starchy foods are not prohibited: they are mainly used to cover energy, training, concentration and recovery.
keyPoints.3: Protein helps with satiety, muscle mass, recovery and day stability.
keyPoints.4: Fats are necessary, but their quantity quickly becomes energy: oil, butter, oilseeds and sauces must be portioned.
keyPoints.5: Regularity counts more than perfection: a simple structure helps to avoid compensations and snacking.

practicalTips.0: Start by stabilizing the main meals before changing all the details.
practicalTips.1: Visualize the plate: 1/2 vegetables, 1/4 protein, 1/4 starch, then measured fat.
practicalTips.2: Adapt the portion of starchy foods according to hunger, physical activity, goal and weight change.
practicalTips.3: Have 2 or 3 easy backup meals for busy days.

equivalences.title: Food equivalences
equivalences.summary: Guidelines for replacing one food with another from the same group without unbalancing the ration.

keyPoints.0: Dairy products: 125 g of natural yogurt, 100 g of cottage cheese, 2 natural petit-suisses or 30 g of cheese can represent a portion depending on the objective.
keyPoints.1: Bread and starchy foods: around 40 g of bread can replace 100 g of cooked starchy foods; 60 g of bread replaces around 150 g of cooked starchy foods.
keyPoints.2: Cooked starchy foods: 150 to 180 g of rice, pasta, semolina, wheat, quinoa or potatoes often correspond to a standard portion.
keyPoints.3: Raw starchy foods: 50 to 60 g of raw pasta/rice/semolina yield approximately 150 to 180 g cooked depending on cooking.
keyPoints.4: Legumes: 150 g cooked lentils, chickpeas or beans can replace a portion of starchy foods and also provide protein.
keyPoints.5: Fat: 10 g of oil, 10 g of butter/margarine or 15 g of oilseeds represent a portion of fat.
keyPoints.6: Fruits: 1 apple, 1 pear, 1 orange, 2 kiwis, 150 g of red fruits or 150 g of compote without added sugar often represent a portion.
keyPoints.7: Meat/fish/eggs: 100 to 120 g of meat/fish, 2 eggs or 150 g of tofu can represent a protein portion depending on the context.
keyPoints.8: Cheese: when cheese is planned, it is often easier to combine it with bread and reduce the starchy foods in the meal.
keyPoints.9: Changing foods within the same group helps maintain adherence without changing the entire ration.

practicalTips.0: Choose an equivalence in the same food group before modifying the total quantities.
practicalTips.1: If you add bread to the meal, reduce the portion of rice, pasta, semolina or potatoes.
practicalTips.2: If cheese replaces yogurt, monitor the lipids and salt more.
practicalTips.3: Keep the quantity indicated at the start, then adjust according to hunger, digestion, objective and progress.
practicalTips.4: Prepare a personal list of 3 preferred equivalences per group to make shopping easier.
practicalTips.5: In diabetes, check the impact of carbohydrate equivalences with the context of the meal, not just weight.

hydration.title: Hydration
hydration.summary: Simple guidelines for distributing water throughout the day and adapting intake around exercise.

keyPoints.0: Generally aim for 1.5 to 2 L of water per day, to be individualized depending on heat, sweating and activity.
keyPoints.1: Drinking regularly works better than compensating with large volumes at once.
keyPoints.2: During short or moderate exercise, water is most often sufficient.
keyPoints.3: After a long, intense or very sweaty effort, think about mineralized water and sodium intake.
keyPoints.4: Sugary drinks are not a daily hydration drink.
keyPoints.5: In renal failure, heart failure or medical instructions, follow the prescribed fluid restriction.

practicalTips.0: Install a visual marker: graduated bottle, flask at the office or glass at each meal.
practicalTips.1: Distribute: 1 to 2 glasses upon waking up, then small doses morning/afternoon.
practicalTips.2: Add lemon, mint, cucumber or red fruits if plain water is difficult.
practicalTips.3: Monitor urine color, headaches, fatigue and cramps as field signals.

indice-glycemique.title: Glycemic index
indice-glycemique.summary: Helps choose and combine carbohydrates for more stable blood sugar levels and better satiety.

keyPoints.0: The glycemic index depends on the food, but also on cooking, grinding and association with the meal.
keyPoints.1: Fiber, protein and fat often slow the absorption of carbohydrates.
keyPoints.2: Juices, sugary drinks and very refined products rise faster than whole foods.
keyPoints.3: Heavily cooked or blended starchy foods can have a quicker impact than an al dente or whole-grain version.
keyPoints.4: In diabetes, the fruit is preferable whole, in portions, and rarely isolated.
keyPoints.5: The context of the meal matters more than a GI classification learned by heart.

practicalTips.0: Combine starch + vegetables + protein rather than starch alone.
practicalTips.1: Favor wholemeal bread, legumes, oatmeal, brown rice or al dente pasta if tolerated.
practicalTips.2: Limit sugary drinks outside of hypoglycemia.
practicalTips.3: Test individual responses with capillary blood glucose or sensors if the patient has them.

sans-gluten.title: Gluten-free diet
sans-gluten.summary: Practical guidelines for removing gluten while maintaining a structured diet.

keyPoints.0: Gluten is present in wheat, barley, rye, spelt and their derivatives.
keyPoints.1: The mention organic, artisanal or complete does not mean gluten-free.
keyPoints.2: Naturally gluten-free foods: rice, corn, quinoa, buckwheat, millet, potatoes, legumes.
keyPoints.3: Processed products may contain hidden gluten: sauces, breadings, cold meats, prepared meals.
keyPoints.4: In celiac disease, cross-contamination is a real issue.
keyPoints.5: Industrial gluten-free products may be lower in fiber and higher in sugars or fats.

practicalTips.0: Read the ingredient list and look for gluten-free if necessary.
practicalTips.1: Separate toaster, board, colander and containers if sensitivity is high.
practicalTips.2: Vary gluten-free starchy foods instead of replacing only with gluten-free bread/pasta.
practicalTips.3: Monitor fiber, iron, magnesium and satiety during follow-up.

sans-lactose.title: Lactose-free diet
sans-lactose.summary: Helps to limit lactose without losing protein, calcium and food pleasure.

keyPoints.0: Lactose intolerance often depends on dose and individual tolerance.
keyPoints.1: Yogurts and mature cheeses can sometimes be better tolerated than milk.
keyPoints.2: Plant-based drinks are not equal: some are low in protein or not enriched with calcium.
keyPoints.3: Lactose can be present in desserts, cookies, prepared meals, sauces and supplements.
keyPoints.4: Eliminating all dairy products is not always necessary if tolerance allows targeted choices.
keyPoints.5: Calcium must be monitored, especially in pregnant, breastfeeding, senior women or athletes.

practicalTips.0: Test gradually: lactose-free milk, yogurt, mature cheese, enriched alternatives.
practicalTips.1: Preferably choose alternatives enriched with calcium and vitamin D.
practicalTips.2: Maintain a protein source if dairy is removed from the meal.
practicalTips.3: Note symptoms, dose and context to avoid overly broad exclusions.

diabete.title: Diabetes and carbohydrate balance
diabete.summary: Guidelines for securing carbohydrates, avoiding peaks and keeping a realistic ration.

keyPoints.0: Avoid sugary drinks on a daily basis, except specifically in cases of hypoglycemia.
keyPoints.1: Limit fruits to consistent portions and pair them with the meal or a source of fiber/protein.
keyPoints.2: Distribute starchy foods throughout the day according to the validated ration.
keyPoints.3: Favor foods rich in fiber if digestion allows it.
keyPoints.4: Sweet products must remain exceptional and integrated into the overall strategy.
keyPoints.5: Symptoms, treatments and activity schedules can modify needs.

practicalTips.0: Build each meal around vegetables + protein + measured starch.
practicalTips.1: Prefer whole fruit over juice or sweet compote.
practicalTips.2: Avoid fruit alone as a snack if blood sugar is unstable.
practicalTips.3: Plan a clear approach for hypoglycemia with the medical team if necessary.

hypertension.title: Hypertension and salt
hypertension.summary: Guidelines for reducing sodium without making the diet dull or difficult to follow.

keyPoints.0: Visible salt is only part of daily sodium.
keyPoints.1: Bread, cheeses, cold meats, prepared meals, broths and sauces are often important sources.
keyPoints.2: Herbs, spices, garlic, onion, lemon and vinegar help maintain flavor.
keyPoints.3: Waters highly mineralized in sodium are not suitable for all hypertensive profiles.
keyPoints.4: The reduction must remain gradual to improve adhesion.
keyPoints.5: For medical treatment, do not use substitute salt rich in potassium without medical advice.

practicalTips.0: Compare labels on bread, ready meals and sauces.
practicalTips.1: Limit cold meats and salty cheeses during the week.
practicalTips.2: Taste before re-salting.
practicalTips.3: Build a list of favorite aromatic seasonings.

hypercholesterolemie.title: Hypercholesterolemia
hypercholesterolemie.summary: Benchmarks for improving fat quality and increasing useful fiber.

keyPoints.0: Limit butter, cream, cold meats, fried foods and ultra-processed products.
keyPoints.1: Favor vegetable oils, nuts/seeds in appropriate portions and fish according to taste.
keyPoints.2: Soluble fibers are interesting: oats, legumes, fruits, vegetables.
keyPoints.3: Weight loss, physical activity and quitting smoking can enhance the dietary effect.
keyPoints.4: Eggs should not be systematically removed, but their frequency must remain consistent.
keyPoints.5: The overall quality of the meal is as important as the individual food.

practicalTips.0: Use olive or rapeseed oil in controlled quantities.
practicalTips.1: Include a portion of vegetables with each main meal.
practicalTips.2: Replace part of the fatty proteins with fish, poultry, legumes or tofu depending on your profile.
practicalTips.3: Monitor fiber and digestion during gradual increases.

digestif-rgo-fodmap.title: Digestive disorders, GERD and FODMAP
digestif-rgo-fodmap.summary: Guides to adjust volumes, textures and irritating foods without excluding them too quickly.

keyPoints.0: Digestive symptoms often depend on dose, stress, sleep and meal speed.
keyPoints.1: In GERD, large meals, alcohol, late meals and fatty foods can increase discomfort.
keyPoints.2: FODMAPs should ideally be worked on in phases, not removed randomly.
keyPoints.3: Raw vegetables, legumes and very fibrous products may require progression.
keyPoints.4: Cooked, tender or split textures are sometimes better tolerated.
keyPoints.5: Too broad a restriction can reduce fiber, calcium, iron and food enjoyment.

practicalTips.0: Note symptoms, meals, time, stress and sleep for 7 to 14 days.
practicalTips.1: Test cooking, peeling, mixing or small portions before completely removing.
practicalTips.2: Avoid lying down immediately after a meal with GERD.
practicalTips.3: Reintroduce gradually to identify true tolerance.

renal.title: Renal monitoring
renal.summary: Cautionary guidelines for renal profiles, which must be adapted to the stage and biological assessments.

keyPoints.0: Protein, potassium, phosphorus, sodium and water requirements depend on the kidney stage.
keyPoints.1: The instructions must follow biological assessments and medical advice.
keyPoints.2: Waters, salt substitutes, supplements and protein powders can be problematic.
keyPoints.3: Certain plants rich in potassium are not prohibited for everyone, but must be contextualized.
keyPoints.4: Ultra-processed foods often contain added sodium and phosphates.
keyPoints.5: The ration must remain individualized, especially in dialysis or advanced renal failure.

practicalTips.0: Check the latest medical advice before changing proteins or potassium.
practicalTips.1: Limit highly processed products and savory broths/sauces.
practicalTips.2: Do not add a complement without validation.
practicalTips.3: Record fluid intake if a restriction is prescribed.

vegetarien-vegan.title: Vegetarian/vegan
vegetarien-vegan.summary: Guidelines for covering proteins and micronutrients in a plant-based diet.

keyPoints.0: Protein should be spread out over the day, not concentrated in one meal.
keyPoints.1: Legumes, tofu, tempeh, soy, cereals and oilseeds combine according to tolerance.
keyPoints.2: As a strict vegan, vitamin B12 must be supplemented.
keyPoints.3: Iron, zinc, calcium, iodine, omega-3 and vitamin D deserve special attention.
keyPoints.4: Not all plant-based alternatives are rich in protein.
keyPoints.5: Food volumes can become high if proteins are poorly distributed.

practicalTips.0: Provide an identified protein source at each main meal.
practicalTips.1: Choose drinks or plant-based yogurts enriched with calcium if used.
practicalTips.2: Combine vitamin C and plant iron sources.
practicalTips.3: Monitor satiety, digestion and actual intake after a few weeks.

grossesse-allaitement.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
grossesse-allaitement.summary: Safety benchmarks and coverage of needs during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

keyPoints.0: Needs vary according to trimester, weight, activity, appetite and symptoms.
keyPoints.1: Folate, iron, iodine, calcium, vitamin D and omega-3 are frequent points of vigilance.
keyPoints.2: Avoid alcohol and microbiological risk products according to medical recommendations.
keyPoints.3: Fish: aim for good quality by avoiding species too rich in mercury.
keyPoints.4: When breastfeeding, hydration, energy and dietary regularity are very important.
keyPoints.5: Supplements must be validated by the referring healthcare professional.

practicalTips.0: Divide if nausea, reflux or rapid satiety.
practicalTips.1: Keep a protein source at each meal.
practicalTips.2: Provide simple snacks if needs increase.
practicalTips.3: Adapt advice to blood tests and medical follow-up.

perte-poids.title: Weight loss
perte-poids.summary: Benchmarks for creating a realistic deficit without sacrificing satiety or food quality.

keyPoints.0: The deficit must remain sustainable and compatible with activity, sleep and hunger.
keyPoints.1: Protein and vegetables often help with satiety.
keyPoints.2: Starchy foods are not prohibited: their quantity and timing are adjusted.
keyPoints.3: Fats are useful but must be portioned.
keyPoints.4: Sugary drinks and liquid snacks can be heavy without filling you up.
keyPoints.5: Adherence matters more than a single perfect day.

practicalTips.0: Identify meals where hunger is greatest before reducing.
practicalTips.1: Keep a stable structure: breakfast if useful, complete main meals.
practicalTips.2: Plan simple alternatives for restaurants, weekends and unforeseen events.
practicalTips.3: Track waistline, energy, hunger and performance, not just weight.

prise-masse-sport.title: Mass gain and performance
prise-masse-sport.summary: Guidelines for increasing intake without making meals unrealistic.

keyPoints.0: The energy surplus must be progressive to limit unnecessary fat gain.
keyPoints.1: Carbohydrates support training, proteins support recovery.
keyPoints.2: Lipids help to densify meals but should not replace all food quality.
keyPoints.3: Timing around training can help if sessions are intense or frequent.
keyPoints.4: Liquid or semi-liquid snacks can help if appetite is low.
keyPoints.5: Sleep remains a major factor in progression.

practicalTips.0: Add a simple snack first before bulking up on main meals.
practicalTips.1: Combine starch + protein in the post-workout meal.
practicalTips.2: Use flakes, muesli, fruit, dairy products or plant-based alternatives according to tolerance.
practicalTips.3: Reassess weight, measurements and performance every 2 to 4 weeks.

proteines-sport.title: Protein supplements for athletes
proteines-sport.summary: Guidelines for choosing a protein powder or gainer without replacing the real ration.

keyPoints.0: Whey is mainly used to supplement an insufficient protein intake or one that is difficult to achieve with meals.
keyPoints.1: Concentrated whey often contains a little more lactose; the isolate is generally more filtered and better tolerated in cases of sensitivity.
keyPoints.2: Casein is slower to digest and can be useful as a long snack, but is not required.
keyPoints.3: Plant proteins may be suitable for vegetarians/vegans, provided you check the actual protein dose per serving.
keyPoints.4: A gainer provides proteins + carbohydrates + calories: it is useful especially if the appetite is too low when gaining mass.
keyPoints.5: Shakers should not systematically replace complete meals: they complement a dietary strategy.

practicalTips.0: Common dose: 20 to 30 g of protein per dose, to be adjusted according to the targeted daily total.
practicalTips.1: Timing: after training, as a snack or at breakfast if it helps achieve the protein target.
practicalTips.2: To gain mass, start by increasing your food intake before adding a high-calorie gainer.
practicalTips.3: If you have lactose intolerance, prefer isolate, hydrolyzate or adapted vegetable protein.
practicalTips.4: Check ingredients, sweeteners, digestibility and anti-doping certification if competition.
practicalTips.5: Avoid in case of renal pathology without medical validation.

creatine.title: Creatine
creatine.summary: Guidelines for using creatine monohydrate for strength, power and recovery.

keyPoints.0: Creatine monohydrate is the most studied and generally the most relevant form.
keyPoints.1: It can help with repeated efforts, strength, power and sometimes lean mass gain.
keyPoints.2: It does not replace training, energy intake or sleep.
keyPoints.3: A slight weight gain linked to intracellular water is possible.
keyPoints.4: The charging phase is not obligatory.
keyPoints.5: Caution is necessary in renal pathology or medical treatment.

practicalTips.0: Single dose: 3 to 5 g per day, every day.
practicalTips.1: Moment: the most important thing is regularity; around a meal or after training if it makes the habit easier.
practicalTips.2: Drink enough and avoid multiplying products that already contain creatine.
practicalTips.3: Choose pure creatine monohydrate, ideally tested/certified if competing.

bcaa-eaa.title: BCAA/EAA
bcaa-eaa.summary: References to understand the real interest of amino acids around training.

keyPoints.0: BCAAs alone are rarely helpful if total protein intake is already sufficient.
keyPoints.1: EAAs are more complete than BCAAs, but remain secondary to dietary proteins.
keyPoints.2: They may be of occasional benefit if training is done on an empty stomach or if protein intake is very low.
keyPoints.3: They do not compensate for an insufficient ration in calories or protein.
keyPoints.4: Marketing often overestimates their impact on recovery.
keyPoints.5: In practice, a well-placed meal or whey is often more effective and simpler.

practicalTips.0: Priority: reach daily protein target before adding BCAA/EAA.
practicalTips.1: If used: follow the dose of the product, often 5 to 10 g around training.
practicalTips.2: Avoid versions that are very sweet or rich in stimulants if this is not desired.
practicalTips.3: Reserve for cases where eating or drinking a complete protein is difficult.

citrulline.title: Citrulline
citrulline.summary: Benchmarks for strength sports, intense sessions and search for muscle congestion.

keyPoints.0: Citrulline may support nitric oxide production and feelings of congestion.
keyPoints.1: It is mainly used before weight training sessions or intense efforts.
keyPoints.2: The effect depends on the dose, regularity and digestive tolerance.
keyPoints.3: It does not replace carbohydrates, hydration or warming up.
keyPoints.4: It can be present in pre-workouts with caffeine and other active ingredients.
keyPoints.5: Caution in case of cardiovascular treatment or unstable blood pressure.

practicalTips.0: Common dose: 6 to 8 g of L-citrulline or citrulline malate approximately 30 to 60 min before session.
practicalTips.1: Start lower if digestion is sensitive.
practicalTips.2: Avoid accumulating several pre-workouts without checking the total doses.
practicalTips.3: Test in training, never for the first time on the day of a competition.

l-carnitine.title: L-carnitine
l-carnitine.summary: Realistic benchmarks on L-carnitine, often sold as a fat burner.

keyPoints.0: L-carnitine is not a magic fat burner.
keyPoints.1: Its effect on weight loss is generally modest and depends mainly on the overall energy deficit.
keyPoints.2: It may be of interest in certain specific contexts, but it is not a priority.
keyPoints.3: Sleep, protein, fiber, activity and eating regularity often have more impact.
keyPoints.4: Combined slimming products may contain caffeine or stimulants.
keyPoints.5: Digestive tolerance must be monitored.

practicalTips.0: If used: often 1 to 2 g per day depending on product and tolerance.
practicalTips.1: Do not use this as a justification for excessively reducing intake.
practicalTips.2: Check the stimulants associated with slimming formulas.
practicalTips.3: Reassess interest after a few weeks based on objective criteria.

fruits-legumes-saison.title: Seasonal fruits and vegetables
fruits-legumes-saison.summary: Guides to increase variety, fiber and food pleasure thanks to the seasons.

keyPoints.0: Seasonality helps vary colors, textures and micronutrients.
keyPoints.1: Plain frozen foods are a good alternative out of season.
keyPoints.2: Raw foods and raw foods do not have the same digestive tolerance.
keyPoints.3: The fruits remain to be portioned according to the objective and pathologies.
keyPoints.4: Vegetables can be included in soup, pan-fried, light gratin, salad or side dish.
keyPoints.5: Variety matters as much as quantity.

practicalTips.0: Choose 2 seasonal vegetables and 2 fruits to try each week.
practicalTips.1: Alternate raw/cooked according to digestion.
practicalTips.2: Prepare a base of cooked vegetables for 2 to 3 days.
practicalTips.3: Use herbs, spices and lemon to avoid monotony.

sommeil.title: Improve sleep
sommeil.summary: Nutritional and behavioral benchmarks to support sleep and recovery.

keyPoints.0: A dinner that is too heavy, too fatty or too late can interfere with falling asleep.
keyPoints.1: Caffeine can remain active for several hours depending on the person.
keyPoints.2: Alcohol often degrades sleep quality despite initial drowsiness.
keyPoints.3: Too much food restriction can increase nighttime hunger or awakenings.
keyPoints.4: The regular rhythm of meals helps some patients stabilize energy.
keyPoints.5: Excessive hydration just before bed can increase nighttime awakenings.

practicalTips.0: Test a caffeine limit in the early/mid afternoon.
practicalTips.1: Plan a digestible dinner with protein, vegetables and suitable starchy foods if hungry at night.
practicalTips.2: Avoid large fluid intakes in the hour before bedtime.
practicalTips.3: Note sleep, dinner time, alcohol, caffeine and training to spot the links.

anti-age.title: Anti-aging diet
anti-age.summary: Benchmarks to support metabolic health, muscle mass and dietary quality over time.

keyPoints.0: The priority remains a regular diet, rich in varied plants and sufficient protein.
keyPoints.1: Muscle mass is protected with proteins, physical activity and recovery.
keyPoints.2: Fiber supports microbiota, cholesterol and satiety.
keyPoints.3: Omega-3, vitamin D, calcium and antioxidants may be points of vigilance.
keyPoints.4: Ultra-processed products, excessive alcohol and a sedentary lifestyle often accelerate imbalances.
keyPoints.5: Prevention must remain adapted to pathologies and treatments.

practicalTips.0: Include a protein source with each main meal.
practicalTips.1: Vary the plant colors during the week.
practicalTips.2: Integrate fish, nuts/seeds or alternatives depending on your profile.
practicalTips.3: Monitor strength, energy, sleep and digestion as you age.

complements.title: Food supplements
complements.summary: Guidelines for using supplements only when they meet a real need.

keyPoints.0: A supplement does not replace an unbalanced ration.
keyPoints.1: The needs should ideally be objective: biological assessment, symptoms, sporting or medical context.
keyPoints.2: Interactions with treatments exist, especially plants, minerals and high doses.
keyPoints.3: In pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or heart disease, increased caution.
keyPoints.4: Protein powder, creatine, vitamin D, omega-3 or magnesium are not useful for everyone.
keyPoints.5: The quality of the product, dosage and duration are as important as the choice of supplement.

practicalTips.0: List all supplements already taken before adding one.
practicalTips.1: Check objective, dose, duration and stopping criteria.
practicalTips.2: Favor dietary corrections when they are sufficient.
practicalTips.3: Request medical validation in the event of treatment or pathology.

tca.title: Eating disorders
tca.summary: Points of caution to accompany without reinforcing control or guilt.

keyPoints.0: The priority is safety, the therapeutic alliance and multidisciplinary work.
keyPoints.1: Numerical targets can be sensitive and should be used with caution.
keyPoints.2: Rigid restrictions can worsen food compulsions, avoidance or anxiety.
keyPoints.3: Eating regularity is often more important than nutritional perfection.
keyPoints.4: Moral vocabulary around food should be avoided.
keyPoints.5: Gravity signals require specialized medical guidance.

practicalTips.0: Favor simple and reassuring guidelines rather than a list of prohibitions.
practicalTips.1: Assess hunger, satiety, emotions and context without judgment.
practicalTips.2: Do not impose food weighing if it increases anxiety.
practicalTips.3: Work in conjunction with a doctor, psychologist or psychiatrist if necessary.
